study type: Observational study, nested within a randomised controlled trial
outcome: Cesarean section for failed instrumental delivery
cohort: 478 nulliparous women at term (≥37 weeks of gestation) undergoing instrumental delivery
finding: Suboptimal instrument placement during delivery was associated with increased maternal and neonatal morbidity, as well as a greater likelihood of procedural complications, such as the use of sequential instruments and cesarean section for failed instrumental delivery.
mod_finding: While the study doesn't directly compare modes of delivery, it finds that suboptimal instrument placement during instrumental delivery is associated with increased procedural complications, including cesarean section for failed instrumental delivery.
